rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph answers the brothers’ confession and admission of guilt by removing blame and reproach from them.
rows.anchor: لما اعترفوا بفضله عليهم وبكونهم مجرمين خاطئين قال يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathrīb means reproach or fault-finding; its root is tharb, the fat covering the stomach, and the verb suggests removing it.
rows.anchor: أي لا توبيخ ولا عيب وأصل التثريب من الثرب

rows.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that after an enslaved woman receives the prescribed punishment, she must not be taunted for fornication.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إذا زنت أمة أحدكم فليضربها الحد

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: It is easier to ask young people for help than elders, as Joseph absolves his brothers while Jacob says he will seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء الخراساني طلب الحوائج إلى الشباب أسهل منها إلى الشيوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading connects today to the denial of reproach: if there is no reproach on this especially blameworthy day, there will be none on other days.
rows.anchor: إنه متعلق بقوله : { لا تثريب } أي لا أثر بكم اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, today marks Joseph’s present ruling of universal absolution: denying reproach as a kind denies every instance across times and circumstances.
rows.anchor: نفي للماهية ونفي الماهية يقتضي انتفاء جميع أفراد الماهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph then asks God to remove their punishment in the afterlife; God forgive you is a supplication.
rows.anchor: لما بين لهم أنه أزال عنهم ملامة الدنيا طلب من الله أن يزيل عنهم عقاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading connects today to forgiveness: God accepted their repentance and forgave them that day after their shame, confession, and return.
rows.anchor: لما انكسروا وخجلوا واعترفوا وتابوا فالله قبل توبتهم وغفر ذنبهم

rows.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: At the conquest of Mecca, the Prophet asked Quraysh what they thought he would do and answered with Joseph’s words of absolution.
rows.anchor: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام أخذ بعضادتي باب الكعبة يوم الفتح

rows.speaker: العباس
rows.claim: Abbas told Abu Sufyan to recite Joseph’s words when approaching the Prophet; the Prophet prayed that God forgive Abu Sufyan and his teacher.
rows.anchor: أن أبا سفيان لما جاء ليسلم قال له العباس

rows.speaker: يوسف عليه السلام
rows.claim: When his brothers felt ashamed to dine with him because of their past mistreatment, Joseph said their visit now honored him and made Egyptians recognize his kinship to Abraham.
rows.anchor: إن أهل مصر وإن ملكت فيهم فإنهم ينظروني بالعين الأولى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes say Joseph learned that his father had lost his sight after asking the brothers about him, then gave them his shirt.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : لما عرفهم يوسف سألهم عن أبيه فقالوا ذهبت عيناه

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The critical exegetes say Joseph knew by revelation that placing the shirt on Jacob’s face would restore his sight, since reason alone could not establish it.
rows.anchor: قال المحققون : إنما عرف أن إلقاء ذلك القميص على وجهه يوجب قوة البصر بوحي من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A natural explanation is possible: grief and crying weakened Jacob’s sight, while the shirt’s joyful effect strengthened his spirit and eyesight; medical principles support this.
rows.anchor: فإن القوانين الطبية تدل على صحة هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يأت بصيرا can mean he will become sighted, supported by the later wording he returned sighted.
rows.anchor: أي يصير بصيرا ويشهد له { فارتد بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means that Jacob will come to Joseph able to see; he is singled out for honor, while the others are all to be brought.
rows.anchor: ويقال : المراد يأت إلي وهو بصير ، وإنما أفرده بالذكر تعظيما له

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi estimates Joseph’s family at about seventy people.
rows.anchor: قال / الكلبي : كان أهله نحوا من سبعين إنسانا

rows.speaker: مسروق
rows.claim: Masruq says the group entering Egypt with Joseph numbered ninety-three men and women.
rows.anchor: وقال مسروق دخل قوم يوسف عليه السلام مصر . وهم ثلاثة وتسعون من بين رجل وامرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Judah carried the shirt, wanting to bring Jacob joy as he had caused grief by carrying the bloodstained shirt.
rows.anchor: روي أن يهودا حمل الكتاب وقال أنا أحزنته بحمل القميص الملطخ بالدم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Judah carried the shirt barefoot and bareheaded from Egypt to Canaan, a journey of eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: وقيل حمله وهو حاف وحاسر من مصر إلى كنعان وبينهما مسيرة ثمانين فرسخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph sent two hundred camels of provisions; he and the king, with four thousand troops and Egypt’s dignitaries, went out to meet Jacob, who walked leaning on Judah.
rows.anchor: روي أن يوسف عليه السلام وجه إلى أبيه جهازا ومائتي راحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same account Jacob mistook the approaching royal party for Pharaoh; after Judah identified Joseph, Jacob greeted him because Joseph had been prevented from greeting first.
rows.anchor: فقال يعقوب عليه السلام : السلام عليك وقيل إن يعقوب وولده دخلوا مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report counts Jacob’s household entering Egypt as seventy-two people and the fighting men who later left with Moses as 600,570, excluding children and elders.
rows.anchor: أن يعقوب وولده دخلوا مصر وهم اثنان وسبعون ما بين رجل وامرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes his parents literally as father and mother; some say his mother was alive, others that she had died and God raised her to fulfill the dream.
rows.anchor: المراد أبوه وأمه ، وعلى هذا القول فقيل إن أمه كانت باقية حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the second parent as Jacob’s aunt: Rachel died after Benjamin’s birth, and Jacob married her sister, whom scripture calls a parent because an aunt can stand as a mother.
rows.anchor: المراد أبوه وخالته ، لأن أمه ماتت في النفاس بأخيه بنيامين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aunt can be called a parent either because she fills the mother’s role or because a maternal aunt is like a mother, just as an uncle is like a father.
rows.anchor: لأن الخالة أم كما أن العم أب ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { وإلاه آبائك إبراهيم وإسماعيل وإسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awā ilayhi means he drew his parents close and embraced them.
rows.anchor: آوى إليه أبويه ضمهما إليهما واعتنقهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their entering before Egypt means Joseph met them at a nearby house or tent, welcomed them, and then told them to enter Egypt.
rows.anchor: كأنه حين استقبلهم نزل بهم في بيت هناك أو خيمة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Joseph spoke before their entry because he had already gone out to meet them.
rows.anchor: قال السدي إنه قال : هذا القول قبل دخولهم مصر ؛ لأنه كان قد استقبلهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets enter Egypt as settle there safely, with residence expressed as entry because the two are paired.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : المراد بقوله : { ادخلوا مصر } أي أقيموا بها آمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation attaches if God wills to safety, as in the promise of entering the Sacred Mosque safely in 48:27.
rows.anchor: أنه عائد إلى الأمن لا إلى الدخول ، والمعنى : ادخلوا مصر آمنين إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation attaches if God wills to entering, since Joseph said this before they entered Egypt.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه عائد إلى الدخول على القول الذي ذكرناه إنه قال لهم هذا الكلام قبل أن دخلوا مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safe means secure in persons, property, and family, with no fear of anyone; formerly they feared Egypt’s kings.
rows.anchor: يعني على أنفسكم وأموالكم وأهليكم لا تخافون أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations say they were promised safety from famine, hardship, and poverty, or from Joseph’s retaliation for their old crime.
rows.anchor: وقيل آمنين من القحط والشدة والفاقة ، وقيل آمنين من أن يضرهم يوسف بالجرم السالف

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: The linguists define the throne as an elevated couch or seat, citing the Queen of Sheba’s great throne in 27:23.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : العرش السرير الرفيع قال تعالى : { ولها عرش عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration raises a problem because Jacob was Joseph’s father, elderly, and a prophet of higher standing; filial duty and age should have made Joseph honor him.
rows.anchor: يعقوب عليه السلام كان أبا يوسف وحق الأبوة عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s prostration-to-God reading fits the dream if the family prostrated for Joseph’s sake, seeking his benefit and elevation; Razi deems it necessary given the father’s superior age, knowledge, religion, and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن هذا التأويل متعين ، لأنه لا يستبعد من عقل يوسف ودينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection says that reading the family’s prostration as gratitude for finding Joseph does not match the dream’s image of sun, moon, and stars prostrating to him.
rows.anchor: فإن قالوا : فهذا التأويل لا يطابق قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dream’s words can mean that sun and moon prostrated for Joseph’s sake, seeking his welfare and rank, rather than worshipping him.
rows.anchor: من قوله : { والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لى ساجدين } لأجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another good answer makes Joseph like the qibla: the family prostrated to God toward him in gratitude for finding him.
rows.anchor: جعلوا يوسف كالقبلة وسجدوا لله شكرا لنعمة وجدانه

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan’s poetry supports saying that one prays toward or for the qibla, supporting the expression of prostrating toward Joseph as qibla.
rows.anchor:
قال حسان شعرا :
ما كنت أعرف أن الأمر منصرف … عن هاشم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer takes prostration as humility, as in poetry describing hills bowing to hooves; the objection is that falling suggests a full prostration, but fall can also mean pass over, as in 25:73.
rows.anchor: ترى الأكم فيها سجدا للحوافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth answer says the pronoun in they fell to him refers to Joseph’s brothers and other visitors, not his parents, who were raised onto the throne in honor.
rows.anchor: بل الضمير عائد إلى إخوته ، وإلى سائر من كان يدخل / عليه لأجل التهنئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dream’s interpretation need not reproduce its imagery exactly: the family’s journey from Canaan to Egypt to honor Joseph fulfills the dream’s symbolism of elders honoring him.
rows.anchor: فسجود الكواكب والشمس والقمر ، تعبير عن تعظيم الأكابر من الناس له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fifth answer treats prostration as the customary greeting, but Razi rejects it as very unlikely: Jacob, not Joseph, would then more properly receive the prostration.
rows.anchor: وهذا في غاية البعد لأن المبالغة في التعظيم كانت أليق بيوسف منها بيعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth possibility is that Jacob prostrated because his brothers’ pride would otherwise revive old grudges; his public action removed their resistance, like a ruler allowing an inspector to discipline him.
rows.anchor: حتى تصير مشاهدتهم لذلك سببا لزوال الأنفة والنفرة عن قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh answer is that God commanded Jacob for a hidden wisdom, as He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam; Joseph disliked it inwardly but stayed silent because he knew it was commanded.
rows.anchor: لعل الله تعالى أمر يعقوب بتلك السجدة لحكمة خفية لا يعرفها إلا هو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the parents’ and brothers’ prostration startled Joseph and made his skin bristle; he told Jacob the dream had now been fulfilled.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إنه لما رأى سجود أبويه وإخوته هاله ذلك واقشعر جلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reaction supports the divine-command interpretation: a prophet’s dream is true and may impose an obligation, as Abraham’s dream led to the commanded sacrifice.
rows.anchor: فإن رؤيا الأنبياء حق كما أن رؤيا إبراهيم ذبح ولده صار سببا لوجوب ذلك الذبح عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi suggests the prostration may have completed Jacob’s severe test: after years longing for Joseph, he had to prostrate upon reunion.
rows.anchor: إنك كنت دائم الرغبة في وصاله ودائم الحزن بسبب فراقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes give the interval between the dream and its fulfillment as eighty, seventy, forty years (the majority view), or eighteen years.
rows.anchor: فقيل ثمانون سنة ، وقيل : سبعون ، وقيل : أربعون ، وهو قول الأكثرين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan’s chronology says Joseph entered the well at seventeen, endured eighty years of slavery and prison, reunited with his family, then lived twenty-three more years and died at 120.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه ألقي في الجب وهو ابن سبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsana bī means God acted kindly toward me; the phrase is also used as a construction with ilā, as in poetry by Kathir.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { وقد أحسن بى } أي إلي يقال : أحسن بي وإليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph mentions release from prison but omits the well to avoid reproaching his brothers, since recalling the well would revive their guilt.
rows.anchor: ولو ذكر واقعة البئر لكان ذلك تثريبا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the well led to enslavement, whereas leaving prison led to kingship; prison release was therefore the fuller benefit.
rows.anchor: لما خرج من البئر لم يصر ملكا بل صيروه عبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After release from the well Joseph still suffered the woman’s accusation; prison release reunited him with family and ended the accusation.
rows.anchor: لما أخرج من البئر وقع في المضار الحاصلة بسبب تهمة المرأة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says prison was the greater blessing because Joseph entered it due to a desire he had; Razi qualifies this as natural inclination, excusable ordinarily but potentially blameworthy for an intimate of God.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : النعمة في إخراجه من السجن أعظم لأن دخوله في السجن كان بسبب ذنب هم به

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: One interpretation takes al-badw as the open countryside, where a person is visible at a distance; Jacob’s family in Canaan were pastoral nomads.
rows.anchor: وقال الواحدي : البدو بسيط من الأرض يظهر فيه الشخص من بعيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jacob had moved to the place called Bada, where he had a mosque under its mountain, and came from there to Joseph.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كان يعقوب قد تحول إلى بدا وسكنها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari identifies Bada as a known place between Shiʿb and Bada; the place-name reading makes the phrase mean they came from their journey to Bada.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : بدا اسم موضع معروف يقال هو بين شعب وبدا

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kathir’s verse naming Shiʿb and Bada supports treating Bada as a place-name, rather than the countryside.
rows.anchor: وأنت التي حببت شعبا إلى بدا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: On the place-name view, the family were townspeople, and bada means to come to Bada, as ghāra means to go to the lowland.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول كان يعقوب وولده حضريين لأن البدو لم يرد به البادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports the Ashʿarite view that human acts are created by God: Joseph attributes release from prison and the family’s arrival from the countryside to God.
rows.anchor: وهذا صريح في أن فعل العبد بعينه فعل الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi, al-Kaʿbi, and al-Qadi use Joseph’s attribution of beneficence to God but family discord to Satan against determinism.
rows.anchor: احتجوا بهذه الآية على بطلان الجبر

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses Satan’s nudging as corrupting and leading astray; the root evokes a rider goading a mount into motion, or pricking it.
rows.anchor: نزغ } أفسد بيننا وأغوى وأصله من نزغ الراكض الدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers the anti-determinist argument by saying attribution to Satan is figurative: Satan has no coercive power and admits that he only invited people, who responded.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن ظاهر القرآن يقتضي إضافة هذا الفعل إلى الشيطان مع أنه ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan’s sin required another Satan, causation regresses infinitely; if it did not, the same can be said of human sin. Humans do not choose harmful error for its consequences, so God is the remaining cause.
rows.anchor: ولما كان وقوعه في الكفر والفسق لا بد له من موقع / وقد بطل القسمان لم يبق إلا أن يقال ذلك من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding wording also explicitly attributes the whole sequence to God, reinforcing this conclusion.
rows.anchor: الآية المتقدمة على هذه الآية وهي قوله : { إذ أخرجنى من السجن وجاء بكم من البدو } صريح في أن الكل من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is subtle in arranging the unlikely reunion: when He wills something, He gently makes its causes easy despite its apparent remoteness.
rows.anchor: حصول الاجتماع بين يوسف وبين أبيه وإخوته مع الألفة والمحبة وطيب العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s subtle action rests on His knowledge of every possible circumstance and His wise, precise, nonfutile judgment and deeds.
rows.anchor: عليم بجميع الاعتبارات الممكنة التي لا نهاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Joseph showed Jacob his treasure rooms; Jacob reproached him for not writing during the eight-stage journey. Joseph said Gabriel forbade it because Jacob feared the wolf but had not feared God.
rows.anchor: فلما أدخله مخازن القراطيس قال يا بني ما أغفلك ، عندك هذه القراطيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Jacob lived with Joseph twenty-four years, asked burial beside Isaac in Syria, and was buried there by Joseph; Joseph returned to Egypt and lived twenty-three more years.
rows.anchor: أقام معه أربعا وعشرين سنة ولما قربت وفاته أوصى إليه أن يدفنه بالشام إلى جنب أبيه إسحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Joseph then longed for the next life and death; Egyptians disputed his burial, settled on a marble coffin in the Nile so all could receive its blessing, and Moses later recovered and buried his remains by his father.
rows.anchor: فتخاصم أهل مصر في دفنه كل أحد يحب أن يدفه في محلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s descendants are given as Ephraim and Misha, then Nun and Joshua, Moses’ attendant; Joseph’s bones remained in Egypt until Moses removed them.
rows.anchor: وولد له افراثيم وميشا ، وولد لافراثيم نون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle min in some kingdom and some interpretation is partitive because Joseph received only part of worldly rule and interpretive knowledge.
rows.anchor: من في قوله : { من الملك * ومن * تأويل الاحاديث } للتبعيض

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Asamm explains the partitive wording by saying Joseph had someone above him in kingship.
rows.anchor: قال الأصم : إنما قال من الملك ، لأنه كان ذو ملك فوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes God, who acts without being acted upon; bodies, which are affected but do not act; and souls, which receive divine knowledge and affect bodies. Kingdom signals bodily governance, while interpretive knowledge signals connection to divine realities.
rows.anchor: مراتب الموجودات ثلاثة : المؤثر الذي لا يتأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because human degrees of bodily and spiritual perfection are finite, people attain only a portion of each, explaining the partitive min.
rows.anchor: امتنع أن يحصل منهما للإنسان إلا مقدار متناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he learned the meaning of fāṭir when two Bedouins disputed ownership of a well and one said he had originated, or begun digging, it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما كنت أدري معنى الفاطر حتى احتكم إلي أعرابيان في بئر

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Linguists say faṭr originally means splitting or cracking, as with a camel’s tooth emerging, a thing splitting, or plants breaking through earth; it then came to mean bringing something into existence.
rows.anchor: أصل الفطر في اللغة الشق يقال : فطر ناب البعير إذ بدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāṭir does not by itself mean creation from absolute nothing: the heavens were made from smoke, humans from clay, and producing a form from existing matter does not entail creating that matter.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الحق أنه لا يدل عليه ويدل عليه وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pot exists when matter takes a particular form; producing the pot does not prove the maker produced its constituent matter, so the word fāṭir alone does not prove creation of all matter.
rows.anchor: فعلمنا أن كونه موجدا للكون لا يقتضي كونه موجدا لمادة الكوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may suggest that heavens precede earth if the conjunction implies order; reason also says a defined outer sphere implies a center, while one center can have infinitely many surrounding spheres. The plural heavens and singular earth are discussed at 6:1.
rows.anchor: يوهم أن تخليق السموات مقدم على تخليق الأرض عند من يقول

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows Fatir to be accusative as an adjective of the vocative Lord, or as a second vocative.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : نصبه من وجهين : أحدهما : على الصفة لقوله : { رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You are my guardian in both lives means God manages all the speaker’s affairs, linking temporary worldly rule with lasting rule in the next life.
rows.anchor: أنت الذي تتولى إصلاح جميع مهماتي في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports faith and obedience being from God: if they came from the servant, the servant would manage his own interests, contradicting God’s comprehensive bestowal.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الإيمان والطاعة كلمة من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A report from God through Gabriel says that whoever is occupied by remembrance instead of asking receives more than those who ask; accordingly Joseph praises God before supplicating, as Abraham does.
rows.anchor: حكى عن جبريل عليه السلام عن رب العزة أنه قال : ( من شغله ذكري عن مسألتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph first praises God for kingdom, interpretive knowledge, and creating the heavens and earth, then asks to die Muslim and join the righteous.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر عقيبه الدعاء وهو قوله : { توفنى مسلما وألحقنى بالصالحين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada and many exegetes understand Joseph to ask to join God through death; they say no prophet before him had wished for death.
rows.anchor: فقال قتادة : سأل ربه اللحوق به ولم يتمن نبي قط الموت قبله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata’s report, interprets the prayer as asking that when God takes Joseph, He take him in Islam, not as a request for death itself.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : في رواية عطاء يريد إذا توفيتني فتوفني على دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the wording can bear either meaning and argues that a wise person may long for death because finite human knowledge and power cannot reach absolute perfection, leaving the soul in frustrated striving.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد في الرجل العاقل إذا كمل عقله أن يتمنى الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly pleasures are fleeting, their loss hurts more than their acquisition pleases, they are mixed with disturbances, and lower people may possess more of them than the virtuous.
rows.anchor: أن هذه السعادات سريعة الزوال مشرفة على الفناء والألم الحاصل عند زوالها أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest argument, according to the investigators, is that bodily pleasures merely remove pains such as hunger, sexual frustration, or frustrated ambition, making them low and unworthy of attachment.
rows.anchor: أن هذه اللذات الجسمانية لا حقيقة لها ، وإنما حاصلها دفع الآلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Food pleasure is weak beside severe illness, temporary because eating ends hunger, intrinsically base and disgusting in its bodily processes, shared by low animals, dependent on painful hunger, and scorned by the wise.
rows.anchor: من كان همته ما يدخل في بطنه فقيمته ما يخرج من بطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sexual pleasure shares food’s defects and produces children, multiplying material needs and potentially leading people into dangerous schemes to obtain money.
rows.anchor: النكاح سبب لحصول الولد ، وحينئذ تكثر الأشخاص فتكثر الحاجة إلى المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Political authority is hard to obtain because others resist one person’s ambition to command; if obtained, it remains insecure and its loss brings fear and grief.
rows.anchor: على شرف الزوال في كل حين وأوان بكل سبب من الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise person sees no real benefit in worldly pleasures, yet the soul is strongly drawn to them; pursuing them through bodily life therefore means ongoing affliction, so one may wish that life to end.
rows.anchor: ما دام يكون في هذه الحياة الجسمانية فإنه يكون طالبا لهذه اللذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodily pleasures repeat without increasing and become tedious, while afterlife joys have many kinds without end.
rows.anchor: موجبات هذه اللذة الجسمانية متكررة ولا يمكن الزيادة عليها

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Razi says he personally experiences this state and could write volumes on the defects of bodily pleasures, so he often repeats Joseph’s prayer.
rows.anchor: أنا صاحب هذه الحالة والمتوغل فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ashʿarites argue that faith and its preservation come from God: if they came from the servant, asking God to preserve them would be incoherent, like asking someone to do what he does not do.
rows.anchor: من العبد كان طلبه من الله فاسدا

rows.speaker: الجبائي والكعبي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi and al-Kaʿbi answer that Joseph asks God for gracious aid to remain Muslim until death.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي والكعبي معناه : اطلب اللطف لي في الإقامة على الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that answer as departing from the explicit request for Islam; moreover, God has already granted every possible form of gracious aid, so asking for it would be impossible.
rows.anchor: فهذا الجواب ضعيف لأن السؤال وقع على السلام فحمله على اللطف عدول عن الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although prophets know they will die Muslim, the prayer can seek a fuller Islam: settled surrender, contentment with God’s decree, and a peaceful, open heart, beyond mere non-disbelief.
rows.anchor: كمال حال المسلم أن يستسلم لحكم الله تعالى على وجه يستقر قلبه على ذلك الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes take joining the righteous to mean joining Joseph’s forefathers Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob in their reward and ranks.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وغيره من المفسرين : يعني بآبائه إبراهيم وإسمعيل وإسحق ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi poses the objection that a great prophet who has surpassed the first rank of righteousness should not ask for that beginning rank.
rows.anchor: والصلاح أول درجات المؤمنين ، فالواصل إلى الغاية كيف يليق به أن يطلب البداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An esoteric interpretation says compatible departed souls exchange divine lights like polished mirrors reflecting sunlight to one another, amplifying radiance beyond weak eyesight.
rows.anchor: انعكس النور الذي في كل واحدة منها إلى الأخرى بسبب تلك الملازمة والمجانسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative is the subject and the unseen-report clause its predicate; Muhammad was not with Joseph’s brothers when they resolved their plan and schemed against him.
rows.anchor: كنت عند إخوة يوسف { إذ أجمعوا أمرهم } أي عزموا على أمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account is a miracle: Muhammad did not read books, study under anyone, or live among scholars, yet told a long, accurate story without distortion or error.
rows.anchor: إتيانه بهذه القصة الطويلة على وجه لم يقع فيه تحريف ولا غلط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that Muhammad was not there is phrased as a taunt, since everyone knows he was absent from the scene.
rows.anchor: وما كنت لديهم } أي وما كنت هناك ذكر على سبيل التهكم بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh and a group of Jews demanded the story challengingly; Muhammad hoped it might persuade them, but they persisted in unbelief, recalling that guidance is God’s to give in 28:56.
rows.anchor: كفار قريش وجماعة من اليهود طلبوا هذه القصة من رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the conditional clause has an omitted apodosis, since a conditional answer cannot precede its condition.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : جواب { لو } محذوف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ gives the normal verbal form for striving and notes a rare dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء في ( المصادر ) يقال : حرص يحرص حرصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet seeks no payment, while the Qur’an reminds all people of monotheism, justice, prophethood, resurrection, stories, obligations, and worship; rational people should accept it.
rows.anchor: إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين } أي هو تذكرة لهم في دلائل التوحيد والعدل والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is no surprise that people ignore proofs of the Prophet when they also pass by the abundant signs of God’s oneness, power, and wisdom throughout the world.
rows.anchor: لا عجب إذا لم يتأملوا في الدلائل الدالة على نبوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Celestial signs include the spheres’ measured dimensions and arrangement, and their motions, whose temporal beginning implies a capable mover; speed, slowness, and direction also indicate design.
rows.anchor: فقد يستدل بمقاديرها المعينة على وجود الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stars indicate a maker through their size, position, motion, colors, lights, and effects in producing light, shadow, darkness, and brightness.
rows.anchor: وأما الأجرام الكوكبية فتارة يستدل على وجود الصانع بمقاديرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Terrestrial signs include wonders of land and sea, atmospheric phenomena, diverse minerals, plants with distinct qualities, animals’ varied forms and voices, and human anatomy and faculties.
rows.anchor: فإما أن تكون مأخوذة من بسائط ، وهي عجائب البر والبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rise and disappearance of ancient kings who ruled, devastated lands, and conquered people, leaving only burden and punishment, is another sign.
rows.anchor: ثم بقي الوزر والعقاب عليهم هذا ضبط أنواع هذه الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a full account of the upper and lower worlds exceeds human reason, God refers to their signs in broad terms.
rows.anchor: والعقل البشري لا يفي بالإحاطة به فلهذا السبب ذكره الله تعالى على سبيل الإبهام

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Zamakhshari reports a nominative reading of earth as the subject of they pass over it; al-Suddi reads it accusative as an object of traverse, while Ibn Masʿud’s codex has earth as subject with they walk upon it.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) قرىء { والارض } بالرفع على أنه مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many acknowledged God as creator yet assigned worship to others; the verse’s believers are thus polytheists in worship despite recognizing God.
rows.anchor: أنهم كانوا مقرين بوجود الإله بدليل قوله : { ولئن سألتهم من خلق * السماوات والارض ليقولن الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas identifies the verse’s people as those who liken God to created things.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هم الذين يشبهون الله بخلقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says it concerns pagan Arabs’ talbiya, which acknowledged one God but excepted a partner owned by Him along with what that partner owned.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في تلبية مشركي العرب لأنهم كانوا يقولون : لبيك لا شريك لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists groups’ mixed confessions: Meccans made angels God’s daughters, idolaters treated idols as intercessors, Jews and Christians assigned divine sons, and sun and moon worshippers called them lords; emigrants and Helpers confessed God alone.
rows.anchor: وقال عبدة الأصنام : ربنا الله وحده والأصنام شفعاؤنا عنده

rows.speaker: الكرامية
rows.claim: The Karramiyya infer that faith is verbal confession alone because God calls these people believers despite their polytheism.
rows.anchor: واحتجت الكرامية بهذه الآية على أن الإيمان عبارة عن الإقرار باللسان فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi dismisses the Karramiyya’s inference with a brief, unspecified rebuttal.
rows.anchor: وجوابه معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ghashiya is punishment that envelops and spreads over them; the Hour’s sudden arrival is unexpected, and the closing phrase reinforces its suddenness.
rows.anchor: أي عقوبة تغشاهم وتنبسط عليهم وتغمرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghtatan is an adverbial state-form; the verb means that an event surprised them when they did not expect it.
rows.anchor: وبغتة نصب على الحال يقال : بغتهم الأمر بغتا وبغتة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes take the path as Muhammad’s invitation, way, practice, and method; religion is called a path because it leads to reward, as in 16:125.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : قل يا محمد لهم هذه الدعوة التي أدعو إليها والطريقة التي أنا عليها سبيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word path literally means a road; beliefs are likened to roads by which a person reaches paradise.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن السبيل في أصل اللغة الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad and his followers invite to God through insight, proof, and answering doubts; this requires certainty, otherwise the invitation is delusion.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الدعاء إلى الله تعالى إنما يحسن ويجوز مع هذا الشرط

rows.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying describes scholars as trustees of the messengers for God’s servants because they preserve what people are called to.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( العلماء أمناء الرسل على عباد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative syntax ends the first clause at invite to God and begins a new statement: I and my followers are upon clear insight.
rows.anchor: وقيل أيضا يجوز أن ينقطع الكلام عند قوله { ادعوا * إلى الله } ثم ابتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glory be to God coordinates with this is my way as another command to proclaim God’s transcendence from partners; the Prophet disavows the polytheists.
rows.anchor: سبيلى } أي قل هذه سبيلي وقل سبحان الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that dialectical theology and the foundations of religion are prophetic vocations and part of why prophets were sent.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تدل على أن حرفة الكلام وعلم الأصول حرفة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings are nūḥī with nūn for Hafs from Asim and yūḥī with yāʾ for the other readers; Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hafs read address-form taʿqilūn, while the rest read third-person yaʿqilūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم { نوحى } بالنون ، والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the claim that God would send an angel, the verse answers that earlier messengers too were human men receiving revelation in towns; it also excludes women and inhabitants of the wilderness from messengership.
rows.anchor: من جملة شبه منكري نبوته عليه الصلاة والسلام أن الله لو أراد إرسال رسول لبعث ملكا

rows.speaker: الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying states that one who lives in the wilderness grows coarse, and one who follows hunting becomes heedless.
rows.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من بدا جفا ومن اتبع الصيد غفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travelers are asked to inspect the ruins and fate of earlier peoples who denied their messengers.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { أفلم يسيروا فى الارض فينظروا } إلى مصارع الأمم المكذبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode of the Hereafter means the final state’s abode, like the expression first prayer for the first obligatory prayer; its superiority was argued earlier.
rows.anchor: ولدار الاخرة خير } والمعنى دار الحالة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read the light form kadhabū with kasra on dhāl; the other readers use the intensified form.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي { كذبوا } بالتخفيف ، وكسر الذال والباقون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the light reading, one view makes the people the subject: after the messengers lost hope, the people suspected the promised victory was a lie; the people are inferable from mention of messengers or of earlier deniers in 12:109.
rows.anchor: أي حتى إذا استيأس الرسل من إيمان القوم فظن القوم أن الرسل كذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second light-reading view makes the messengers think they themselves had been lied to about victory; Razi calls it remote because believing God lies would invalidate a prophet’s faith.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المعنى أن الرسل ظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا فيما وعدوا

rows.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Mulayka transmits from Ibn Abbas the view that the messengers thought they had been lied to, due to human weakness.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل منقول عن ابن أبي مليكة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the intensified reading, one view takes assume as know: the messengers knew their peoples had definitively rejected them, so they prayed against them and annihilating punishment followed; 2:46 uses the verb for certainty.
rows.anchor: أن الظن بمعنى اليقين ، أي وأيقنوا أن الأمم كذبوهم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha’s interpretation, which Razi prefers, is that messengers feared their believing followers had now called them liars after the messengers despaired of the broader people.
rows.anchor: وهذا التأويل منقول عن عائشة رضي الله عنها وهو أحسن الوجوه المذكورة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha rejects Ibn Abbas’s reported claim that prophets thought God had lied to them: God’s promise to Muhammad was known to be fulfilled, though prolonged trials made prophets fear believers would disbelieve them.
rows.anchor: فأنكرته وقالت : ما وعد الله محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا إلا وقد علم أنه سيوفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the crisis reached its limit, God’s help came and He saved whomever He willed.
rows.anchor: لما بلغ الحال إلى الحد المذكور { جاءهم نصرنا فنجى من نشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir read the passive one-nūn form with a doubled jīm and open yāʾ; Abu Ubayda prefers it because the codex has one nūn.
rows.anchor: بنون واحدة وتشديد الجيم وفتح الياء

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: A reading attributed to al-Kisaʾi assimilates one nūn into another, producing one nūn, doubled jīm, and a still yāʾ; some call it erroneous because a vowelled nūn cannot assimilate into a still one or into jīm.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الكسائي : إدغام إحدى النونين في الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers use two nūns with a light jīm and still yāʾ, meaning that God saves them.
rows.anchor: والباقون بنونين ، وتخفيف الجيم وسكون الياء على معنى : ونحن نفعل بهم ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative uses a present-tense expression to depict a past event, as with the past story’s present-tense wording in 28:15.
rows.anchor: حكاية حال ، ألا ترى أن القصة فيما مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtibār is crossing from what is known to what is unknown, meaning reflection and thought.
rows.anchor: الاعتبار عبارة عن العبور من الطرف المعلوم إلى الطرف المجهول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph’s rise from well to prison, from slave to ruler, and reunion with his family after a long separation show that God can likewise exalt Muhammad and his message.
rows.anchor: لقادر على إعزاز محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وإعلاء كلمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story also reports unseen events, making it a miracle and evidence that Muhammad is truthful.
rows.anchor: أن الإخبار عنه جار مجرى الإخبار عن الغيب ، فيكون معجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening calls the account the best of stories and the ending explains why: its beauty lies in yielding lessons and knowledge of wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر في آخرها : { لقد كان فى قصصهم عبرة لاولى الالباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stories most likely means Joseph, his brothers, and his father, though some take it to mean the stories of all prophets previously recounted.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : المراد قصص الرسل لأنه تقدم في القرآن ذكر قصص سائر الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story can be called an admonition for people of intellect because all are able to reflect, or because the praised people of intellect are those who actually reflect and benefit.
rows.anchor: إن جميعهم كانوا متمكنين من الاعتبار ، والمراد من وصف هذه القصة بكونها عبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of not fabricated is that Muhammad could not invent the story because he had not studied books or scholars, while it matches the Torah; another is that the account itself is not false.
rows.anchor: أن المراد الذي جاء به وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يصح منه أن يفتري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an confirms earlier scripture by matching the Torah and other divine books; confirmation is accusative with an elided predicate, though a nominative reading meaning it is confirmation is also grammatical.
rows.anchor: ويجوز رفعه في قياس النحو على معنى : ولكن هو تصديق الذي بين يديه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ, along with al-Zajjaj, allows the grammatical analysis that confirmation is nominative, meaning rather it is confirmation of what came before.
rows.anchor: قاله الفراء والزجاج ، ثم قال : ويجوز رفعه في قياس النحو
